content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early cycles, especially when sentiment is bullish.", "Sentiment spikes often precede sharp price drops, indicating model lag in capturing sentiment-driven reversals.", "Models show mean-reversion bias in later cycles, underestimating sustained price trends.", "High sentiment volatility correlates with forecast overshoots, suggesting sentiment should be weighted more heavily in calibration.", "Forecast accuracy declines when sentiment is mixed or negative, indicating sentiment interaction is critical for model adjustment.", "Models fail to capture sharp downward trends when sentiment turns bearish, suggesting lag in sentiment-to-price response.", "Forecast bias is more pronounced in low-volume periods, requiring dynamic model recalibration.", "Sentiment-driven corrections are often missed by models, leading to persistent forecast errors in volatile regimes."]}
